# Use case 1: gene coexpression and regulatory networks

Here, we will use __GraphExperiment__ to store gene-gene networks inferred
from bulk RNA-seq data. We will use the maize (*Zea mays*) gene expression
data set distributed with the __BioNERO__ package [@almeida2022bionero],
which contains 28 samples from different tissues [@shin2021network].
From these data, we will infer a gene coexpression network (GCN) and a
gene regulatory network (GRN), and store both in the `rowGraphs` slot of
a `GraphExperiment` object.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(here)
library(GraphExperiment)
library(BioNERO)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggraph)
library(patchwork)

set.seed(123) # for reproducibility
```
:::


## Data description and processing

The expression data are stored in a `SummarizedExperiment` object with
a gene expression matrix (in TPM) and sample metadata. **BioNERO** also
contains a data frame with maize transcription factors (TFs), which we
will use to infer the GRN.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Load data
data(zma.se)
data(zma.tfs)

zma.se
```

To keep this example lightweight, we will remove lowly expressed genes
and keep only the top 2,000 most variable genes. We will also use
`exp_preprocess()` to remove outlier samples and adjust for confounders.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Preprocess data and keep only the top 2,000 most variable genes
exp <- exp_preprocess(
    zma.se, min_exp = 10, variance_filter = TRUE, n = 2000
)

exp
```

## Gene coexpression network inference

Next, we will infer a GCN with the WGCNA algorithm [@langfelder2008wgcna] as
implemented in __BioNERO__. First, we need to pick the power
$\beta$ to which correlation coefficients will be raised to make the
network fit a scale-free topology.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Pick power for scale-free topology fit
sft <- SFT_fit(exp, net_type = "signed hybrid", cor_method = "pearson")
```

Now, we can infer the GCN.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Infer the GCN
gcn <- exp2gcn(
    exp, net_type = "signed hybrid", SFTpower = sft$power,
    cor_method = "pearson"
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
..connectivity..
..matrix multiplication (system BLAS)..
..normalization..
..done.
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Number of genes per module
table(gcn$genes_and_modules$Modules)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

    black      cyan darkgreen   darkred      grey    purple       red 
      518       878       245       222        56        42        39 
```


:::
:::


The object returned by `exp2gcn()` contains the adjacency matrix of
the full network, which we will convert to an `igraph` object. Note that
we will __not__ filter edges here. The adjacency matrix represents a
complete, weighted graph, with edge weights representing the
(soft-thresholded) coexpression between gene pairs. Then, we will add
module assignments and intramodular connectivities as node attributes.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Convert adjacency matrix to an igraph object
gcn_graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
    gcn$adjacency_matrix, mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE
)

# Add module assignments and intramodular degree as node attributes
nodes <- V(gcn_graph)$name
modules <- setNames(gcn$genes_and_modules$Modules, gcn$genes_and_modules$Genes)
V(gcn_graph)$module <- modules[nodes]
V(gcn_graph)$kWithin <- gcn$kIN[nodes, "kWithin"]

# Identify hub genes and add them as node attributes
hubs <- get_hubs_gcn(exp, gcn)
V(gcn_graph)$is_hub <- nodes %in% hubs$Gene

gcn_graph
```

The result is an `igraph` object with vertex (or node) attributes `name`,
`module`, `kWithin`, and `is_hub`, and an edge attribute `weight`.

## Gene regulatory network inference

Now, we will infer a GRN using the 'wisdom of the crowds' approach
implemented in `exp2grn()`, which combines the results of GENIE3, ARACNE,
and CLR [@huynh2010inferring; @margolin2006aracne; @faith2007large]
and selects the top edges that make the network best fit a
scale-free topology.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Get TFs among the top 2,000 most variable genes
tfs <- intersect(zma.tfs$Gene, rownames(exp))
length(tfs)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 31
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Infer GRN
grn_edges <- exp2grn(exp, regulators = tfs, nTrees = 1000)
head(grn_edges)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
         Regulator         Target
285 Zm00001d041474 Zm00001d012007
280 Zm00001d041474 Zm00001d006602
291 Zm00001d041474 Zm00001d027374
282 Zm00001d041474 Zm00001d008691
288 Zm00001d041474 Zm00001d015811
304 Zm00001d042263 Zm00001d045042
```


:::
:::


GRNs typically include only a subset of the genes, as genes that are not
regulated by any TF (or that are not TFs) are not included in the
edge list. However, `GraphExperiment` requires that nodes in row graphs
match row names *exactly*. Thus, when creating the `igraph` object, we will
include all genes as nodes, and genes that are not in the GRN
will be represented as isolated nodes.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create a directed graph from the edge list, including all genes as nodes
grn_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(
    grn_edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = data.frame(name = rownames(exp))
)

grn_graph
```

## Storing networks in a `GraphExperiment` object

Now that we have both networks, we can store them in a `GraphExperiment`
object along with the expression data and sample metadata. We will also
add gene-level metadata indicating whether each gene encodes a TF.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Add gene-level metadata to `rowData`
rowData(exp)$is_TF <- rownames(exp) %in% zma.tfs$Gene
rowData(exp)$TF_family <- zma.tfs$Family[match(rownames(exp), zma.tfs$Gene)]

# Create a `GraphExperiment` object
ge <- GraphExperiment(
    assays = assays(exp),
    colData = colData(exp),
    rowData = rowData(exp),
    rowGraphs = list(gcn = gcn_graph, grn = grn_graph)
)

ge
```

Note that node attributes in each graph are automatically added to
`rowData`, with column names in the format `<graph name>__<attribute>`.
This way, module assignments, intramodular degree, and hub status
can be accessed (and used, e.g., for subsetting) as any other
feature-level metadata.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

```

## Exploring the networks

Since all data are stored in a single object, subsetting is straightforward.
For example, let's subset the object to keep only genes in the module
with the largest number of TFs. Subsetting a `GraphExperiment`
object subsets assays, `rowData`, and all graphs in `rowGraphs`
simultaneously.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Get the module with the largest number of TFs
tfs_per_module <- table(rowData(ge)$gcn__module[rowData(ge)$is_TF])
tfs_per_module
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

    black      cyan darkgreen   darkred      grey       red 
       14         9         2         2         1         3 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
top_module <- names(which.max(tfs_per_module))

# Subset the object to keep only genes in this module
ge_mod <- ge[rowData(ge)$gcn__module == top_module, ]
ge_mod
```

:::


Finally, let's visualize the coexpression and regulatory networks for
genes in this module, highlighting TFs and hub genes. For visualization
purposes, we will only display the strongest coexpression edges.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Extract graphs from the subset object (with `rowData` as node attributes)
g_gcn <- rowGraph(ge_mod, "gcn")
g_grn <- rowGraph(ge_mod, "grn")

# Keep only top 5% edges in the GCN (for visualization only)
w <- E(g_gcn)$weight
g_gcn <- delete_edges(g_gcn, which(w < quantile(w, 0.95)))

# Remove isolated nodes from both graphs (for visualization only)
g_gcn <- delete_vertices(g_gcn, which(degree(g_gcn) == 0))
g_grn <- delete_vertices(g_grn, which(degree(g_grn) == 0))

# Plot GCN, with node size proportional to intramodular degree
p_gcn <- ggraph(g_gcn, layout = "fr") +
    geom_edge_link(aes(alpha = weight), color = "grey60", show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_node_point(aes(size = kWithin, color = is_hub)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey40", `TRUE` = "firebrick")) +
    theme_graph(base_family = "sans") +
    labs(
        title = paste0("Coexpression network (module '", top_module, "')"),
        color = "Hub gene", size = "Intramodular degree"
    )

# Plot GRN, highlighting TFs
p_grn <- ggraph(g_grn, layout = "fr") +
    geom_edge_link(
        arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm")), end_cap = circle(1.5, "mm"),
        color = "grey60"
    ) +
    geom_node_point(aes(color = is_TF, size = is_TF)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey40", `TRUE` = "steelblue")) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1.5, `TRUE` = 4)) +
    theme_graph(base_family = "sans") +
    labs(
        title = paste0("Regulatory network (module '", top_module, "')"),
        color = "TF", size = "TF"
    )

wrap_plots(p_gcn, p_grn, nrow = 1) +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](chapter_01_files/figure-pdf/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){fig-pos='H'}
:::
:::


Because module assignments, hub status, and TF annotation travel
together with the graphs, any downstream analysis (e.g., finding TFs
that are hubs in both networks) can be done with standard
`SummarizedExperiment` syntax.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# TFs that are also GCN hubs, with their out-degree in the GRN
rowData(ge) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    rownames_to_column("gene") |>
    filter(is_TF, gcn__is_hub) |>
    mutate(grn_outdegree = degree(rowGraph(ge, "grn"), gene, mode = "out")) |>
    select(gene, TF_family, gcn__module, gcn__kWithin, grn_outdegree)
```
